lastCompletedStory.title: Add absence/presence oracle idiom to the planner Oracle Contract

nextStoryContext: US-001 added a new paragraph to the Oracle Contract section in BOTH .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/agents/subagent-planner.md (right after the [oracle: ...] examples list, before '## Mandatory Acceptance Criteria'): the absence/presence idiom ('! grep -q PATTERN file' for absence, 'grep -q PATTERN file' for presence, never combine -q with -L/-l -- self-nullifying). Re-embedded via `bun run embed-vendor`; extended test/embedded.test.ts's 'templatesContents — oracle contract in planner prompt (US-001)' describe block with a new test asserting the idiom text. Raised test/embedded.test.ts's file-size-budget.json ceiling 653->659 (actual line count via content.split('\n').length) with a dated _ref note citing CAM-309/US-001. US-002 (next, same PRD) targets the AUDITOR prompt instead (.claude/agents/subagent-auditor.md + templates/agents/subagent-auditor.md, section 'C. Acceptance criteria health' ~line 60-72): it must make the auditor BLOCK when it sees the -q+-L/-l antipattern in ANY order/spacing (-Lq, -qL, -L -q, -lq), not just the literal '-Lq' string. Both stories regenerate the same src/vendor/_generated.ts, so US-002 must re-run `bun run embed-vendor` again after its own edit (drift check is stateless, not cumulative across stories). Do not touch scripts/cam/patterns.md's existing CAM-301 bullet (~line 767) documenting the -Lq oracle bug: it already covers the root cause this PRD is hardening against.
